source.title: A Precise High-Dimensional Asymptotic Theory for Boosting and Min-L1-Norm Interpolated Classifiers

record.file_problem: Complete paper text; some mathematical notation and typography show extraction artifacts.
record.tranche_reason: The study analyzes generalization error for boosting and minimum-ℓ1-norm interpolated classifiers while varying the feature-to-sample ratio. This bears on general double descent across model classes, but uses a different model and method from deep-network double descent.
record.gate_note: The paper cites a separate study on double descent, but cited results are not recorded as rows. It reports its own generalization-error results across p/n; the reported plots do not provide recoverable numerical values or a textual description of a fall-rise-fall shape.
record.test_reason: The study computes the min-ℓ1-norm interpolant's (boosting limit) generalization error as overparametrization ψ=p/n varies, in theory and simulation. That bears on V4 for a non-deep model class. The analysis covers only the separable regime ψ>ψ*(≈0.43 in Fig. 1). The text never states the error curve's shape, so no verdict can be drawn.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors give exact asymptotic formulas for the max-ℓ1-margin, the min-ℓ1 interpolant's generalization error and its relation to Bayes error, and the boosting iteration threshold. They find overparametrization speeds optimization and that finite-sample simulations match the theory. They draw no double-descent conclusion; double descent appears only in a citation of Deng et al. (peak at the separability threshold).
record.recipe_differences: High-dimensional asymptotic analysis and simulations of boosting/minimum-ℓ1-norm interpolated classifiers, rather than deep-network size, epoch, or sample-size sweeps.
record.method_sensitivity: The study varies ψ and ρ in its plots and compares Rademacher with moment-matched Gaussian covariates; the text describes close agreement between the latter settings, not a change in double-descent outcome.

fits_no_version.finding: The iteration threshold T(n) for boosting to approach the min-ℓ1 interpolant decreases as ψ grows. The authors say 'overparametrization leads to faster optimization'.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Overparametrization speeds the optimization of boosting to the max-margin interpolant.

fits_no_version.finding: The scaled max-ℓ1-margin κ*/√ψ increases with ψ (Figure 2), which bounds the fraction of active features at interpolation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Larger overparametrization yields larger normalized margins and sparser interpolating boosting solutions.

record.problems: The generalization-error results relevant to V4 are mostly shown in figures, without recoverable numerical values or a textual account of curve shape. The characterization applies under stated asymptotic assumptions; finite-sample plots average over 10 runs in Figure 1 and two runs in Figure 3, with no error bars or other uncertainty reported.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant reported risk-sweep results omitted.

untested.parts: Whether risk peaks at the interpolation threshold and falls again beyond it. Only ψ above the separability threshold is analysed, and the curve's shape is never stated.
Test error over boosting iterations is not reported; only the iteration threshold T(n) is.
Sample-size effects at fixed p are not examined.
No effective-complexity measure is used to predict peak location.
Label noise, multiple peaks and optimal regularization are not examined.
Effective parameter counting is not examined.

record.verdict_notes: Relation is kept as tests (T2) only because the plotted error-vs-ψ curves could in principle bear on V4. In practice the paper is a precise-asymptotics characterization restricted to ψ>ψ*, and every row is cannot_determine, so no verdict is given. If plot values were digitized, a decline of error with ψ above the threshold would at most speak to the post-interpolation part of V4, not the peak.

versions.untested_parts: Deep-network test error as model size grows and its peak near the training-set interpolation size.
Test error over training epochs or boosting iterations.
Increasing the number of training samples near the interpolation threshold.
Whether risk improves again after the interpolation point: the text gives a generalization-error formula and plots, but does not state the curve shape in words or provide recoverable plotted values.
A single effective-complexity measure predicting peak location across size, epochs, and sample size.
Whether label noise or variance drives a peak, whether multiple peaks occur, or whether optimally tuned regularization removes it.
Whether counting effective parameters turns the second descent into an ordinary U-shaped curve.

relation.reason: The study reports its own risk characterizations and capacity sweeps for minimum-ℓ1-norm classifiers; these bear on V4 beyond its citation of earlier double-descent work.

tranche.reason: High-dimensional asymptotic analysis and simulations characterize classification risk as p/n varies, providing a different method relevant to V4, although the recorded results cannot establish its curve shape.

source_check.notes: The theory assumes separability; the Figure 1 example has threshold approximately 0.43. Risk-curve shapes are not stated in the supplied text, so cannot_determine states and no verdicts are justified.
